lines.text: Do you know why photos get blurry when you send them in a chat?
You snap a sunset. Twelve megapixels, every tiny detail.
To save space, the photo gets chopped into tiny squares, eight pixels by eight.
Each square is rewritten as a mix of simple patterns, from smooth to super fine.
Then the finest patterns, the ones your eye barely notices, get thrown away. That's the squeeze.
Many chat apps squeeze your photo again before sending it. Squeeze it twice, and the edges go blocky.
Orbi Transfer sends the original file, byte for byte. Locked on your phone, full quality on theirs.
